messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The DOI/URL exactly matches the source metadata provided: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12302-023-00716-5.

The status 'comparable_with_conditions' is consistent with the data: all three PFAS (PFBA, PFPeA, PFHxA) were tested on the same weak-base resin D5706, in the same real groundwater, with the same 10% breakthrough criterion, and bed volumes as a common metric, allowing conditional comparability of relative affinity and run length.

The reason cites common column, groundwater matrix, and 10% breakthrough definition, which are all stated or implied in WEB01-E05, and correctly explains why the results are comparable under those shared conditions.

The endpoint is 10% breakthrough bed volumes in a fixed-bed ion-exchange column, which is a measure of removal performance (onset of breakthrough), so classifying the endpoint type as 'removal' is appropriate and consistent with WEB01-E05.

WEB01-E05 reports 10% breakthrough bed volumes for several PFCAs in a column test; the interpretation that this indicates dynamic removal performance and order of breakthrough matches this description.
'10% breakthrough bed volumes' is a direct and accurate phrasing of the metric described in WEB01-E05 (10% breakthrough at specified bed volumes).

WEB01-E05 states that column tests with weak-base resin D5706 treated real PFAS-contaminated groundwater, matching the matrix description of real PFAS-contaminated groundwater fed to a weak-base anion-exchange pilot column.
WEB01-E05 explicitly gives an EBCT range (2.4–6 min) for the D5706 column tests, so naming this operating condition 'Empty bed contact time (EBCT)' is accurate.
WEB01-E05 reports an EBCT of 2.4–6 min, matching the recorded value '2.4-6'.
EBCT is given in minutes in WEB01-E05; using 'min' as the unit is correct.
The qualifier that this EBCT range applies during pilot column operation with D5706 resin is consistent with the description in WEB01-E05 of column tests using D5706 at EBCT 2.4–6 min.
WEB01-E05 describes results at '10% breakthrough', so defining a 'Breakthrough criterion' operating condition is appropriate.
The text specifies '10% breakthrough'; recording the value as 10 is consistent with this criterion.
The criterion is defined as a percentage of the influent concentration (10% breakthrough), so '% of influent concentration' is an appropriate unit description.
The qualifier that bed volumes at 10% breakthrough are reported for several PFCAs correctly reflects WEB01-E05.
PFBA is explicitly listed in WEB01-E05 as one of the PFAS with reported 10% breakthrough bed volumes.
PFPeA is explicitly listed in WEB01-E05 as one of the PFAS with reported 10% breakthrough bed volumes.
PFHxA is explicitly listed in WEB01-E05 as one of the PFAS with reported 10% breakthrough bed volumes.
WEB01-E05 gives a 10% breakthrough bed volume for PFBA; labeling this finding 'PFBA breakthrough' is an accurate description.

WEB01-E05 reports '10% breakthrough of PFBA at ~4,000 BV.' The recorded value 4000 matches the approximate number, but the source explicitly indicates it is approximate ('~'), while the record uses value_form 'exact_numeric'. The numeric magnitude is supported, but the exactness is overstated.
Bed volumes (BV) are the metric used in WEB01-E05; using 'BV' as the unit is correct.
The qualifier notes that the value is approximate and corresponds to 10% breakthrough for PFBA on weak-base resin D5706, which aligns with WEB01-E05.
WEB01-E05 provides a 10% breakthrough bed volume for PFPeA; 'PFPeA breakthrough' is an accurate label for this value.

WEB01-E05 reports '10% breakthrough of ... PFPeA at ~10,000 BV.' The recorded value 10000 matches the approximate number, but the use of value_form 'exact_numeric' overstates the precision; the magnitude is supported but not exactness.
'BV' correctly reflects the bed volume metric used in WEB01-E05.
The qualifier that this is an approximate bed volume at 10% breakthrough for PFPeA on D5706 is consistent with WEB01-E05.
WEB01-E05 provides a 10% breakthrough bed volume for PFHxA; 'PFHxA breakthrough' is an accurate description.

WEB01-E05 reports '10% breakthrough of ... PFHxA at ~25,000 BV.' The stored value 25000 matches the approximate number, but labeling it as 'exact_numeric' overstates the precision; the numeric level is supported but not its exactness.
'BV' correctly represents the bed volume metric used in WEB01-E05.
The qualifier that these are approximate bed volumes at 10% breakthrough for PFHxA on D5706 matches the description in WEB01-E05.

WEB01-E05 describes column tests with weak-base resin D5706 treating real PFAS-contaminated groundwater with given EBCT; summarizing this as a packed-bed ion exchange column with weak-base anion-exchange resin D5706 operated at varying EBCTs for PFAS removal from groundwater is accurate.

The section label in the evidence refers to an 'IEX pilot column', and WEB01-E05 describes column tests on real groundwater, consistent with pilot-scale ion exchange column tests with a weak-base resin.
Given that the work is described as an 'IEX pilot column' treating real contaminated groundwater, classifying the study as 'pilot_or_field_deployment' is appropriate.

WEB01-E05 indicates tests with a single weak-base resin (D5706) and a single real PFAS-contaminated groundwater; inferring as a design-based limitation that extrapolation to other waters or resins requires caution follows logically from these design facts.

In the provided excerpt (WEB01-E05) only short-chain PFCAs (PFBA, PFPeA, PFHxA) are discussed for the weak-base IEX column. As a design-inferred limitation about the scope captured in the provided results, it is reasonable to note that longer-chain PFAS or PFSAs performance is not captured there.

WEB01-E05 does not discuss resin fouling, regeneration, or PFAS transformation products, but absence of mention in the excerpt does not establish that 'no information was provided' in the study as a whole. This limitation goes beyond what can be inferred from the cited text alone.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements required for synthesis—source identity, groundwater matrix, weak-base resin treatment, EBCT conditions, 10% breakthrough removal endpoint, and quantitative breakthrough bed volumes for PFBA, PFPeA, and PFHxA—are well supported by the cited evidence. Minor issues relate only to precision qualifiers on approximate values and an unsupported residuals/transformations limitation and do not compromise use of the quantitative findings or study characterization.
